lemma: Decision-from-search via zero-marker. Let f: {0,1}^N -> {0,1} be a truth table, s >= 1, and S: {0,1}^N -> {0,1}^L a search circuit for search-MCSP[s] of size g and depth d. Assume (E1) if some circuit of size <= s computes f then S(f) != 0^L; (E2) otherwise S(f) = 0^L. Define D(f) = OR_{i<=L} S(f)_i. Then D decides MCSP[s] on f, and D has size <= g + L and depth <= d + ceil(log2 L) (fan-in 2).

proved_step: Verifier decision lemma. Fix n, N=2^n, s>=1, f in {0,1}^N. Let V(f,C)=1 iff C is a fan-in-2 circuit on n inputs of size <= s computing f. Let decode map an L-bit string to a circuit or to reject. Define Dec(f)=V(f, decode(S(f))). If S is correct on members (f has a size-<=s circuit implies S(f) encodes one), then Dec(f)=MCSP[s](f) for all f. Proof: member case: S(f) encodes a valid circuit, so V=1. Non-member case: no size-<=s circuit computes f, so V=0 for every string, hence Dec=0. E2 is not used. OPEN (gap): the size of V must be N*(log N)^{O(1)} to be harmless against the N(log N)^k target; only poly(N,s) overhead is shown.

proved_step: Sized verifier lemma. Fix n, N=2^n, s>=1. Encode a fan-in-2 circuit C on n inputs with s gates as L = O(s log(n+s)) bits: each gate stores two operand indices in [0, n+s) plus a gate-type bit. Let V(f,y) be the circuit with inputs f in {0,1}^N and y in {0,1}^L that outputs 1 iff y is well-formed, decodes to a circuit C of size <= s on n inputs, and C(a)=f(a) for all a in {0,1}^n. Claim: V has size O(N*s*max(n,s)). Proof: (i) Well-formedness and decoding of y cost O(L log L) gates, which is negligible. (ii) For each of the N points a, evaluate C(a) with a universal evaluator. Keep a value bank of n+s wires (the n inputs, hard-wired as constants for a, plus the s gate outputs). Gate t computes its two operands by multiplexers over the n+s bank wires, costing O(n+s) gates per operand, then one gate. One point costs O(s*(n+s)) gates. (iii) Compare C(a) with f(a): O(1) per point. Total O(N*(s*(n+s)+1)) = O(N*s*max(n,s)). With n = log N and s <= (log N)^c for a fixed c >= 1, this is O(N*(log N)^{2c}) = N*(log N)^{O(1)}. Consequence: if a search circuit S of size N(log N)^k outputs encodings of size-<=s circuits, then Dec(f)=V(f,S(f)) is a decision circuit of size N(log N)^{k'} with k' = max(k,2c)+O(1). By S0002, Dec = MCSP[s] (E2 not used). Contrapositive: no size-N(log N)^{k'} circuit family for decision MCSP[(log N)^c] implies none for search-MCSP at size N(log N)^k. This is the direction the H1 transfer needs.
